solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Head of Tesla having given name after bearing a little more fruit (9, two words)

parts.note: Elon Musk runs the electric car company

indicators.note: only a small portion of the following word is wanted, namely its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word
the Tesla boss's first name

explanation.surface: The Tesla chief, carrying a bit more, is named after a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname comes first, then the given name follows the single letter it bears, so the man's whole name sits either side of one extra M.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet, fragrant variety of melon, a kind of cultivated fruit with a ribbed rind.

clue.text: Rural spot's housing commotion

indicators.note: to house something is to give it shelter within, so one piece holds another

parts.note: moil is an archaic word for a spot or blemish, to defile
a fuss is a commotion

explanation.surface: A quiet country place turns out to be home to a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rural spot' reads as one noun phrase, but the definition is the single adjective; 'spot' is the outer wordplay word, archaic moil meaning to stain.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Indian adjective for provincial or up-country districts, away from the main cities and stations.

clue.text: Carnivorous mammal foremost in stalking perfectly

indicators.note: what is foremost comes at the very front, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word
'to a T' means perfectly

explanation.surface: A predator is shown hunting its prey with flawless skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'to a T' supplies four letters at once, which a solver can miss while looking for a single-word synonym of perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat is a small flesh-eating weasel-family animal, an example of a meat-eating mammal.

clue.text: Last to survive in outfit left on account of rhino

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another, which then surrounds it

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothes, an outfit

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
standard abbreviation
o/a is the bookkeeping abbreviation for on account

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a garment because of a rhinoceros, in a curious safari picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On account of' looks like a phrase meaning because of; split it, and 'on account' is the abbreviation O/A while 'of' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern African name for a variety of the black rhinoceros with a longer second horn.

clue.text: Male friend heading off to dance energetically

indicators.note: with the head taken off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: standard abbreviation
tosh is a Scots word meaning friendly or intimate

explanation.surface: A boyfriend leaves to go and dance wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male friend' looks like one unit, but it is M plus a Scots word; the second word loses its first letter before joining on.
explanation.definitionFit: Moshing is the violent jumping and slamming at rock concerts, a kind of frenzied dancing near the stage.

clue.text: Turning to the left in recess see one grandchild in doorway

indicators.note: to recede is to go back, so in a down light the whole run goes back up the column
one piece placed inside another, which then surrounds it

parts.note: the letter C sounds like the word
the Roman numeral
a portal is a doorway
oe is a Scots word for a grandchild

explanation.surface: Someone in an alcove turns to the left and spots a grandchild standing in the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In recess' looks like a place, but it tells you to read everything after it backwards; oe for a grandchild is Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical term meaning coiling or twisting anticlockwise, leftward, as of spiral shells.

clue.text: Hunting-horn on edge of mouth hasn't succeeded to blow

indicators.note: without success means the abbreviation for succeeded is removed

parts.note: o' is a shortened form of on, as in o'clock
a lip is the edge of the mouth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huntsman puts his horn to his lips but cannot manage to sound it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded' is the genealogical abbreviation S, which drops out of the contraction; 'to blow' just describes what you do with the horn.
explanation.definitionFit: An oliphant is a medieval ivory horn made from an elephant's tusk, sounded in the chase.

clue.text: Dogsbodies perhaps passing off as decorators

indicators.note: passing something off sends it away, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: dogsbody is naval slang for a junior officer

explanation.surface: Menial workers try to pass themselves off as professional decorators.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogsbody normally means a drudge, but in the navy it was a midshipman, so the first two words give a rank; the three letters OFF then go.
explanation.definitionFit: Cake decorators apply sugar coating to cakes, so those who ice are decorating in a specialised sense.

clue.text: Note provided for wheeling bikes

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

indicators.note: a wheel turns round, so the letters swing back on themselves

parts.note: so, as in 'so long as', means provided
for and to are interchangeable in 'a cure for/to'

explanation.surface: A written message is handed over for pushing bicycles along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheeling bikes' reads as pushing them, but 'wheeling' applies only to the two short words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimotos are small racing motorbikes, a type of motorised bike for children and hobbyists.

clue.text: Scottish tribute's part of issue for First Lady

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rent paid in kind, in Scots law

definitions.text: part of issue for First Lady
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the sons of Eve

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of issue' looks like a hidden-word signal, but issue means offspring, and the First Lady is Eve, the first woman, not a president's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are fair: a Scots term for rent paid in produce, and the biblical firstborn son of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: About to be beset by a malaise too upsetting — softening of the bones?

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so one piece goes inside
something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone suffers an unpleasant illness that might be a bone disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter for 'about' goes into the jumbled letters of 'a malaise too'; the question mark admits the definition is a gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical condition where bones lose mineral and become soft, usually through lack of vitamin D.

clue.text: Pancake became very cold but is not zero

indicators.note: the phrase asks for one item in place of another: this word, rather than the symbol for nothing

parts.note: froze means became icy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pancake went chillingly cold, though not quite down to freezing point.
explanation.walkthrough: Z is the mathematical symbol-letter for zero; it is swapped for IS, and the clue's 'zero' is not a nought O as solvers first assume.
explanation.definitionFit: Froise is an old dialect word for a thick pancake or omelette, often with bacon in it.

clue.text: I orate and I broadcast beaming out

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker boasts of making speeches and going on the air, smiling broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' sits naturally beside 'orate' as public speaking, but it is the signal to rearrange the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eradiation is the emission of rays, such as light or heat, radiating outward from a source.

clue.text: Ancient tribe seen in Nice more than once?

indicators.note: only what lies within is seen, so the outer letters at each end are dropped

parts.note: the French Riviera city minus its first letter, as the first copy
the city's name written a second time, keeping only its start

explanation.surface: Some ancient people seem to have turned up repeatedly on the French Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: The hiding place is not printed: 'more than once' tells you to repeat the town's name and look across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic people of eastern Britain, led by Boudicca against Roman rule.

clue.text: Ban about attending college?

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: tapu is the Maori form of taboo, a ban

explanation.surface: A prohibition concerns students going to university.
explanation.walkthrough: Students in Britain are said to be 'up at' Oxford or Cambridge while in residence; the question mark shows the definition needs a college named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up at a university is the British idiom for being in residence there as a student.

clue.text: Pressure on one receiving head of school

parts.note: standard abbreviation in physics
a receptor is something that receives

explanation.surface: Someone at the top of a school is put under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A preceptor is a teacher or instructor, and in older use the principal or master of a school.

clue.text: Decoy duck for each within small group on river

indicators.note: something within something else is inside it, enclosed by it

parts.note: a duck is a cricket score of nought
per means for each, as in miles per hour
the in crowd is an exclusive small set
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A hunter's decoy duck is set out for each little party on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decoy duck' looks like the definition, but 'duck' is the nought in cricket; 'in' as an adjective describes an exclusive clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A roper-in is a swindler's accomplice who lures victims in, a human decoy.

clue.text: One joining desperate loner, withdrawn evasive person

indicators.note: someone desperate is in a wild state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so these letters go backwards

parts.note: a slippery, evasive person is called an eel

explanation.surface: Someone signs up despite being a desperate, introverted loner who avoids company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' reads as an adjective for a shy loner, but it turns the slippery creature round.
explanation.definitionFit: An enrollee is a person who signs up, registering as a member of a course or organisation.

clue.text: Distinctive practices force judge to quit society

indicators.note: whatever quits leaves, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: jism is a slang word for energy or force
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Particular customs make a judge resign from high society.
explanation.walkthrough: J is removed from the slang word for vigour, then S is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Isms are doctrines or distinctive systems of practice, named from the suffix used for creeds and movements.

clue.text: Scottish bar's novel beer that's not bitter

parts.note: a swee is a Scots word for a swinging bar or crane over a fire
a novel is a tale

explanation.surface: A Scottish pub offers a new beer that lacks the usual bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub and 'novel' suggests new, but the bar is a pot-hanging rod and the novel is a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet ale is unhopped or lightly hopped malt liquor, the contrast with the hoppy taste of bitter.

clue.text: Mediocre singer in position to fend off

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another, which then surrounds it

parts.note: seconde is the second parrying position in fencing
an informer who sings to the police is a rat

explanation.surface: A poor vocalist is in a position to ward someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mediocre singer' looks like one phrase, but the singer is a criminal informer, and 'fend off' is fencing's parrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate is an idiom for inferior quality, not of the first class, only middling.

clue.text: Meal including chopped up rump and Japanese dish

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in Britain

indicators.note: something chopped up is cut into bits and mixed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dinner features diced rump steak alongside a Japanese course.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea is the British word for an early evening meal, not just the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is a Japanese preparation of seafood or vegetables fried in light batter.

clue.text: Puppet regime's leader at one time changed …

indicators.note: letters that are changed are moved into a different order
the leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puppet government's former leader has been replaced, with the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puppet regime' is a stock phrase, but 'Puppet' alone is the definition and 'regime' gives just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a kind of puppet worked from above by strings attached to its limbs.

clue.text: … for fear that noblest aristocrat's exiled

indicators.note: someone exiled is sent away, so those letters leave

parts.note: taken as written
a nob is a toff, an aristocrat

explanation.surface: Continuing the puppet regime story, a top noble is banished in case of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noblest' is both the source word and the place where the aristocrat is found, at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lest is a conjunction meaning in case, introducing something to be avoided or feared.

clue.text: Outpouring to encourage onset of tears

parts.note: to spur is to urge on

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A flood of emotion seems to bring on crying.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first, with 'to' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A spurt is a sudden gush or jet of liquid, a burst of flow.

clue.text: House in France I wanted to build in brick

indicators.note: what is wanted is lacking, so that letter is missing

parts.note: maison is French for house
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wished to construct a French house out of brick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I wanted' reads as a wish, but 'wanted' means lacking, so the I is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to mason is to construct with masonry, laying stone or brick work.

clue.text: Sicilian contracts horrify, gang murder tipped to return

parts.note: to appal is to horrify

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards
with its tip taken off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: a hit is a contract killing

explanation.surface: Mafia contracts are horrifying when a gang killing is set to come back on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' suggests mob hits, and the gangland murder does appear, but only in the wordplay, beheaded and turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalti is the Italian plural for public works contracts, notorious in Sicily for mafia rigging.

clue.text: Ancient poplars recalled pleasant Sunday afternoon with son …

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a PSA was a Pleasant Sunday Afternoon, a nonconformist church gathering in Britain
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Old trees bring back memories of a lovely Sunday afternoon spent with a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' qualifies the word, not the trees: asp is an archaic form of aspen; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Asp is an old spelling of aspen, the trembling poplar, so archaic words for these trees.

clue.text: … besides tea spent around Chelsea

indicators.note: what is spent is used up and gone, so those letters disappear

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
the London district wraps around the slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Continuing the Sunday picture, a teatime is spent around a fashionable London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The tea word's three letters sit around the outside of Chelsea, a London district; take them away and the middle remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Else, as in 'anything else', means in addition or besides, an adverb of extra.

clue.text: Settlement's time elapsed

parts.note: a pa is a Maori fortified village, plus the 's
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The village's moment has come and gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S is used as a letter here, not as 'is' or 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Past as an adjective means gone by, the sense of time having slipped away.

clue.text: Horizontal prop close to upright in a lot of soil

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another, which then surrounds it
a lot but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to soil is to sully

indicators.note: the close is the finish, so only the end letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mining support stands beside a post sunk into a quantity of earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soil' looks like a noun for earth, but it is the verb meaning to dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: A stull is a timber laid across a mine working to support the roof or walls.

clue.text: Evergreen regularly colours lilac

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A garden shrub routinely flowers in pale purple.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first letter and every second one after it, across both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Clusia is a genus of tropical trees and shrubs with leathery leaves that stay on all year.

clue.text: List of people to be tried once breaking rules — poor lot

definitions.text: List of people to be tried once

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put back differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sorry bunch who broke the rules are on a list for trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' belongs to the definition, marking a historical Scottish legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Scots law, the porteous roll was the official register of accused persons due for trial at court.

clue.text: US Veep introducing English and European retribution

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it in, so it goes inside

parts.note: JD Vance is US vice-president
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An American vice-president brings in punishment for English and Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: Veep is American slang for vice-president; 'and' here joins the two inserted pieces rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vengeance is punishment inflicted in return for an injury, revenge for a wrong.
